paper.title: Sample-Efficient Learning of Stackelberg Equilibria in General-Sum Games

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning a Stackelberg equilibrium in a two-player general-sum game (equilibrium objective).
unmapped: two players (leader with A actions, follower with B actions); query (a,b) pairs and observe noisy rewards of both players
goal: find leader action approximately maximizing worst-case-best-response value phi_0 up to gap_eps + eps
settings.definition_quote: A general-sum two-player bandit game can be described by a tuple $M=(\mc{A},\mc{B}, r_1, r_2)$ ... The follower observes a (potentially random) reward $r_2(a,b)\in[0,1]$. The leader also observes her own reward $r_1(a,b)\in[0,1]$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Leader action determines an episodic MDP for the follower; Stackelberg equilibrium objective (episodic RL / game).
unmapped: follower plays an episodic tabular MDP with S states, B actions, horizon H determined by leader action
settings.definition_quote: A bandit-RL game is described by the leader's action set $\mc{A}$ (with $|\mc{A}|=A$), and a family of MDPs $M=\set{M^a:a\in\mc{A}}$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Stackelberg equilibrium objective in a two-player general-sum game.
unmapped: two linear reward functions (leader and follower) sharing feature map phi(a,b)
settings.definition_quote: r_1(a,b) = \phi(a,b)^\top \theta_1^\star + z_1,~~~ r_2(a,b) = \phi(a,b)^\top\theta_2^\star+ z_2, ... z_1,z_2 are random noise which we assume are mean-zero and $1$-sub-Gaussian.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning optimal mixed strategy to commit to (Stackelberg equilibrium).
unmapped: leader commits to a mixed strategy; follower best-responds without seeing realized action
settings.definition_quote: A general-sum matrix game with simultaneous play can be described as $M=(\mc{A},\mc{B},r_1,r_2)$ with $|\mc{A}|=A$, $|\mc{B}|=B$, and $r_1,r_2:\mc{A}\times\mc{B}\to[0,1]$

conditions: A = B = 2
failure probability at least 1/3
Bernoulli rewards

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-exact-stackelberg
source.quote: For any sample size $n$ and any algorithm for maximizing $\phi_0$ that outputs an action $\what{a}\in\mc{A}$, there exists a bandit game with $A=B=2$ on which the algorithm must suffer from $\Omega(1)$ error with probability at least $1/3$: $\phi_0(\what{a}) \le \max_{a\in\mc{A}} \phi_0(a) - 1/2$.

results.notes: Bound on suboptimality in exact Stackelberg value phi_0, holding with probability >= 1/3 regardless of n.

conditions: epsilon in (0,1)
guarantee: phi_{eps/2}(a_hat) >= max_a phi_0(a) - gap_eps - eps and b_hat is eps-best response
tuning: N = C log(AB/delta)/epsilon^2 samples per pair

source.label: theorem:nested-bandit
source.quote: For any bandit game and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, Algorithm~\ref{algorithm:bandit} outputs $(\what{a}, \what{b})$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... with $n = \wt{O}\paren{ AB/ \epsilon^2}$ samples ... Further, the algorithm runs in $O(n)=\wt{O}(AB/\epsilon^2)$ time.

results.notes: Accuracy target is gap_eps + eps (not eps).

conditions: epsilon in (0,c), gap g in [0,c)
error g+eps with probability at least 1/3
Bernoulli rewards

source.label: theorem:lower-bound-nested-bandit
source.quote: There exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that the following holds. For any $\epsilon\in(0,c)$, $g\in[0,c)$, any $A,B\ge 3$, and any algorithm that queries $N\le c\brac{AB/\epsilon^2}$ samples and outputs an estimate $\what{a}\in\mc{A}$, there exists a bandit game $M$ on which $\gap_\epsilon=g$ and the algorithm suffers from $(g+\epsilon)$ error ... with probability at least $1/3$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit N <= AB/(864 eps^2).
